user.title: go2rtc
user.description: Address of the go2rtc instance that serves the camera streams, and its API login if go2rtc asks for one.

data_description.url: For example http://192.168.1.10:1984. Put a login in the section below, not in the address.

api.name: go2rtc API login
api.description: Fill in only if go2rtc asks for the login set by api.username and api.password. It asks unless it sees the request come from its own 127.0.0.1: the address above is 127.0.0.1 or localhost on the go2rtc machine itself, not a port published from a Docker container (-p 1984:1984), and local_auth: true is not set. A LAN address or a Docker host name counts as another machine, even when Home Assistant runs on the same one.

data_description.username: api.username from the go2rtc configuration. Empty: no login.
data_description.password: api.password from the go2rtc configuration. Leave it empty if go2rtc sets api.username without a password. After a form error the field comes back empty: left empty, it keeps the password typed before for the same username, unless go2rtc refused that login or the address was invalid and held @.

stream.title: Camera
stream.description: Pick a stream and name the camera. A substream is better: every check decodes a frame with ffmpeg on the Home Assistant machine.

data_description.stream: A stream from the go2rtc configuration.
data_description.name: The name of the device and its entities in Home Assistant.

rtsp.name: go2rtc RTSP server
rtsp.description: Fill in only if go2rtc in Docker publishes RTSP on another port or the go2rtc RTSP server asks for a login.

data_description.port: Empty: the port go2rtc listens on (rtsp.listen, usually 8554). Not the API port 1984.
data_description.username: rtsp.username from the go2rtc configuration. Empty: no login.
data_description.password: rtsp.password from the go2rtc configuration. After a form error the field comes back empty: left empty, it keeps the password typed before for the same username, unless the error was a failed trial check.

reauth_confirm.title: go2rtc API login
reauth_confirm.description: go2rtc refused the API login of {name}, or asks for one and none is saved, so the checks of this camera are paused. Enter api.username and api.password from the go2rtc configuration; the login is tried at the saved go2rtc address before it is saved. Each camera added from this go2rtc asks on its own. If go2rtc has moved, change the address with Reconfigure instead, which also ends this request.

data_description.username: api.username from the go2rtc configuration. Empty: no login.
data_description.password: api.password from the go2rtc configuration. A saved password is not used, since go2rtc refused it, and passwords are not shown. An empty field means no password (go2rtc sets api.username without one); after a form error it keeps the password typed before for the same username, unless go2rtc refused that login.

reconfigure.title: go2rtc connection
reconfigure.description: The settings are saved without a connection check. If go2rtc or its RTSP server is unreachable or the RTSP login is wrong, the camera status becomes "Check failed". If go2rtc refuses the API login, Home Assistant asks for it again.

data_description.url: For example http://192.168.1.10:1984. Put a login in the section below, not in the address.

api.name: go2rtc API login
api.description: Fill in only if go2rtc asks for the login set by api.username and api.password. It asks unless it sees the request come from its own 127.0.0.1: the address above is 127.0.0.1 or localhost on the go2rtc machine itself, not a port published from a Docker container (-p 1984:1984), and local_auth: true is not set. A LAN address or a Docker host name counts as another machine, even when Home Assistant runs on the same one.

data_description.username: api.username from the go2rtc configuration. Empty: no login.
data_description.password: api.password from the go2rtc configuration. Passwords are not shown; leave the field empty to keep the saved one, or the one typed before a form error, while the username stays the same. A new username in place of a saved password needs its password; with no saved password, an empty field means no password (go2rtc sets api.username without one). To drop a saved password but keep the username, clear the username and submit, then open Reconfigure again and enter the username alone.

rtsp.name: go2rtc RTSP server
rtsp.description: Fill in only if go2rtc in Docker publishes RTSP on another port or the go2rtc RTSP server asks for a login.

data_description.port: Empty: the port go2rtc listens on (rtsp.listen, usually 8554). Not the API port 1984.
data_description.username: rtsp.username from the go2rtc configuration. Empty: no login.
data_description.password: rtsp.password from the go2rtc configuration. Passwords are not shown; leave the field empty to keep the saved one, or the one typed before a form error, while the username stays the same. A new username needs its password.

error.api_login: A go2rtc API password needs its username, and a new username in place of a saved password needs its password: an empty field keeps the saved one only for the same username. The username cannot contain a colon.
error.cannot_connect: No proper go2rtc reply at this address: it is unreachable or another service answers.
error.check_failed: go2rtc answers, but the trial check failed: {reason}. Check that the go2rtc RTSP server is on and reachable from Home Assistant, that the RTSP port and login below are right, and that ffmpeg works. "HTTP 401" means the go2rtc API login of the previous step stopped working: start the setup again.
error.checks_busy: Other cameras are being checked and no check slot became free in {seconds} seconds. Try again in a minute.
error.invalid_auth: The go2rtc API refused the login: go2rtc asks for one and it is missing or wrong. Enter api.username and api.password from go2rtc.yaml under "go2rtc API login".
error.invalid_url: Enter an http or https address of go2rtc.
error.reauth_api_login: A go2rtc API password needs its username, and the username cannot contain a colon.
error.reauth_cannot_connect: No proper go2rtc reply at the saved address: it is unreachable or another service answers. If go2rtc has moved, change the address with Reconfigure.
error.rtsp_login: Enter both the RTSP username and the password, or neither.
error.rtsp_login_long: The RTSP username and password are too long: ffmpeg would cut them. Encoded as username:password they must fit in 127 characters, where most symbols take 3 characters each and a non-Latin or accented letter 6 or more. Use a shorter username or password.
error.stream_not_found: go2rtc does not know this stream.
error.url_login: Enter the address without a login; put the go2rtc API username and password in the "go2rtc API login" section below.

abort.already_configured: This go2rtc stream is already added as a camera.
abort.reauth_successful: The go2rtc API login has been updated.

data.same_frames: Identical frames in a row before "frozen"

data_description.scan_interval: How often a frame is taken, from 15 to 3600.
data_description.frame_timeout: How long one check may wait for a frame, from 5 to 60. Longer than this usually gives "Frame timeout", or "Check failed" if go2rtc or its RTSP port stops answering.
data_description.failures: Checks in a row without a valid frame (No stream, Bad frame, Frame timeout) before the connection sensor turns off, from 1 to 10. "Check failed" and "Stream not found" are not counted and do not reset the count.
data_description.same_frames: From 2 to 100, or 0 to turn off the freeze check.
data_description.snapshot_stream: The go2rtc stream that the frame_pulse.snapshot action saves, usually the full-resolution main stream of this camera. The monitored stream is the default. Checks keep using the monitored stream.

error.invalid_same_frames: Enter 0 or a value from 2 to 100.
error.streams_unavailable: go2rtc did not return its stream list, so only the monitored and the saved snapshot streams are offered. The other options can be saved as usual.

api_auth_failed.message: go2rtc refused the API login. Enter the current login when Home Assistant asks for it in Settings > Devices & services.

camera_not_found.message: No Frame Pulse camera has this device or entry.

camera_not_loaded.message: The camera {camera} is not loaded. Check its entry in Settings > Devices & services.

check_cancelled.message: The check was stopped because the camera entry was reloaded. Try again.

monitoring_off.message: Monitoring is off. Turn it on to check the camera.

path_is_folder.message: {path} is a folder: name the file.

path_not_absolute.message: The file name {path} is not an absolute path.

path_not_allowed.message: Cannot write {path}: the folder is not allowed. Add it to allowlist_external_dirs in configuration.yaml, or use a media folder.

snapshot.name: Save snapshot
snapshot.description: Saves one keyframe of a Frame Pulse camera as a JPEG file, taken from go2rtc the way a check takes it, from the snapshot stream set in the camera options. The file is written only when a valid frame arrives and appears whole or not at all. Returns the path and the size of the file.

device_id.name: Camera device
device_id.description: The Frame Pulse camera device. Give the device or the entry, not both.

config_entry_id.name: Camera entry
config_entry_id.description: The Frame Pulse camera entry. Give the device or the entry, not both.

filename.name: File name
filename.description: Absolute path of the JPEG file, a template allowed. The folder must be in allowlist_external_dirs or a media folder; it is created if missing. An existing file is replaced.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long ffmpeg may wait for the frame, from 5 to 60 seconds. The go2rtc API requests around it are not counted. Empty: the frame timeout of the camera options.

quality.name: JPEG quality
quality.description: The ffmpeg -q:v number, from 2 (best) to 31; 2 by default. On one 1080p test frame 2 gave about 360 KB, 3 about 280 KB, 5 about 200 KB, 10 about 125 KB; a busy or noisy picture comes out larger. ffmpeg goes no lower than 2.
